patches.old: Alternatively, note that CD8 has one digit less than CD4, and MHC class I has one chain less (functionally) than class II.
patches.new: Alternatively, use the **rule of 8**: CD8 × MHC class I = 8, and CD4 × MHC class II = 8.
patches.reason: The original mnemonic was incorrect (CD4 and CD8 are both one digit; class I has an α chain plus β2-microglobulin). Replaced with the standard rule of 8.

visual.title: MHC class I vs class II presentation
visual.alt: Two columns of steps. MHC class I: proteins made inside the cell are cut by the proteasome, TAP pumps peptides into the ER, where they are trimmed to 8 to 10 amino acids and load onto MHC class I (alpha chain plus beta-2 microglobulin), and the complex reaches the surface of any nucleated cell, where CD8 cytotoxic T cells recognize it and kill the cell. MHC class II: an antigen-presenting cell takes up outside material, endolysosomal proteases cut it, MHC class II leaves the ER carrying the invariant chain, which is cut to CLIP and exchanged by HLA-DM for a 13 to 25 amino acid peptide, and the complex reaches the surface of dendritic cells, macrophages and B cells for CD4 helper T cells. A footer gives the rule of 8 and notes that dendritic cells can cross-present exogenous antigen on MHC class I.
visual.caption: What a cell makes goes on class I; what an APC eats goes on class II.
